verdict.rationale: Dynadot's own security page documents two-factor authentication, account lock and optional Registry Lock, which covers the 2FA element of a defensible registrar account. Nothing in the pack documents scoped or least-privilege API credentials, or IP allowlisting on API access; separate sandbox keys are environment isolation, not permission scoping. Missing for 10: scoped/permissioned API keys, IP allowlisting for API access, details on 2FA methods (e.g. TOTP or hardware keys), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the registrar account itself is defensible — real 2FA, scoped API credentials, and IP allowlisting on API access

citations.quote: Dynadot offers free domain privacy, account lock, two-factor authentication, and optional Registry Lock to keep your online assets safe.
